newsitem.title: UK: Euro media firm seen buying Blenheim stake.
newsitem.headline: Euro media firm seen buying Blenheim stake.

text.p: Brokers NatWest, acting for a large European media company, has bought a 14.9 percent in British exhibition organiser Blenheim Group Plc, market sources said on Tuesday.

But they said the purchaser intended to be a long term shareholder not a bidder for the group. Trading volume in Blenheim surged on Tuesday as NatWest Securities launched the market raid. By 0907 GMT Blenheim shares were up 47-1/2p at 483.
Early speculation suggested Dutch publishing group VNU or EMAP may be behind the stakebuilding but today's activity was not a prelude to a bid, said sources.
"The company intends to be a long-term shareholder in the business. They're not a bidder," said a source.
United News & Media and Reed-Elsevier have both been linked with a bid for the group since Blenheim said it had received an initial approach from an unnamed company back in June.
No-one at Blenheim was immediately available to comment.
